thread:
Mason: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker change I see a regression in prefix cache hit-rate on prod cluster A. P95 latency for short prompts is up ~18%.
Priya: How big of a hit? numbers?
Mason: From traces: cache hit-rate went from 72% -> 49% for 0-64 token prefix paths. Profiling snippet below.
```
-- sample profile --
time: 2026-03-17T22:14Z
prefix_hits: 4900
prefix_misses: 5100
hit_rate: 0.49
batch_size_median: 4
kernel_selected: fused-attn-v2
```
Eva: interesting — could be key normalization change. Did the kernel change touch cache key canonicalization? @Mason did we change keying in that branch?
Mason: Yes — we landed an optimization that stashes short-seq kvs into a fused layout and adjusted the cache key to include shape/dims so the runtime can route to the right kernel. New key example: `v1::model=gpt-j,sha256=...::shape=1x64`. Old key omitted shape. I missed adding tenant salt.
Liam: Oof. That implies two tenants with identical prompts + shape could collide. Does the hash include tenant id at all?
Mason: No — the hashing step currently uses prompt_text + model + shape but not tenant_id due to an oversight (we assumed global cache for performance). Repro snippet:
```
key_old = sha256(prompt + model)
key_new = sha256(prompt + model + shape)
```
Anya: Security issue: cross-tenant cache entries could leak if one tenant's request hits another's cached response. Do we have per-tenant namespaces or encryption at the value layer?
sec-audit-bot: SEC-AUDIT: cached artifact access should be scoped. Current config: kv-store uses global namespace unless `namespace` set by caller. Verify `namespace` usage in runtime.
Priya: Proposed mitigations: 1) rollback kernel branch (stop regression) 2) quick hotfix: include tenant_id in cache key composition (cheap) 3) HMAC the key with tenant-specific secret on write 4) longer-term: envelope-encrypt values per-tenant. Quickest is #2 but note it'll cause cache misses.
Mason: I can push #2 as a patch in ~30m. Concern: changing key shape will create a warmup storm (massive misses). Need a warmup plan.
Liam: Warmup plan ideas: pre-populate hot prefixes for heavy tenants from historical samples, run a coordinated warmup job to prime Dedicated pools, and do a canary rollout (10% traffic) to observe miss ramp. Also apply temporary throttles per-shard to prevent cascading latency.
Eva: Also recommend envelope encryption at rest + per-tenant key so even if a collision occurs the payload is unreadable. That's a longer rollout but lowers blast radius.
Priya: Operational controls: limit new-miss rate per shard to X rps, fallback to smaller batch sizes to contain P95 spikes, and add a permissive feature-flag to flip keying behavior in runtime.
Anya: This has security impact. I'll open a P0 ticket for cross-tenant cache leakage risk and loop in Security & Infra.
Mason: Patch branch created: `fix/tenant-keying-191876`. I'll add unit tests for key composition and an e2e in staging.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: canary rollout started for patch fix/tenant-keying-191876 to staging at 1918765480.
Priya: After patch we should track: hit-rate (0-64 tokens), P95 latency for short prompts, and new-miss rate. Targets: restore hit-rate >=70% and P95 within +/-3% of baseline.
sec-audit-bot: Reminder: add audit log entries on cache write & read including masked tenant id and key hash. Retain logs for 90 days for forensicability.
Mason: I'll add logging + optional HMAC header and coordinate KMS usage for tenant keys. Will also add a migration plan to pre-populate keys for top 20 tenants.
Anya: Thanks — let's regroup 15 after the push for rollout coordination. @Mason ping when build green.
Mason: Will do. thx :thumbsup:
